supervised person’s life that wishes to participate and can provide a first-hand account of 
the positive progress the supervised person is making.  
(5) A Polygraph is a machine that measures a person’s physiological responses when 
they respond to questions. Polygraph assessments are completed or contracted by the 
sex offender treatment provider as required by PC section 3008(d)(3). 
(b) Persons placed on parole on or after July 1, 2012, required to register pursuant to PC 
sections 290 to 290.023, inclusive, shall successfully complete a sex offender 
management program in accordance with PC section 3008(d). Program participation shall 
be no less than one year, up to the entire period of parole. Participation in the sex offender 
management program is required, regardless of when the qualifying offense was 
committed. 
(c) The sex offender treatment provider prescribes the number of treatment hours per 
week as determined by the supervised person’s risks, needs, responsivity, and offense-
free time in the community.  
(d) Supervised persons may complete a sex offender management program before 
discharge from parole, as contemplated by the PC section 3008(d).

(e) The Containment Team’s review of program completion is solely to determine the 
length of a supervised person’s participation and progress in sex offender treatment. This 
review is independent of whether the supervised person should be discharged from 
parole and the electronic monitoring requirements of the supervised person pursuant to 
PC 3010.10. The CTM schedule shall be as follows: 
(1) The first initial CTM shall be between within 90 and 100 calendar days of from release 
to parole, or within between 90 and 100 calendar days of the supervised person’s 
revocation release date following a release of a supervised person who has spent 90 
days or more in custody. The purpose of this CTM is to determine the most appropriate 
level of parole supervision needed for monitoring the supervised person while in the 
community, in accordance with Section 3573(c). 
(2) The second CTM shall be within nine months following the first CTM (one-year CTM). 
This is the first review to determine whether the supervised person’s sex offender 
management program requirements have been satisfied, completing their statutory 
requirement to successfully complete a sex offender management program. 
(3) All subsequent CTMs shall be at least annually thereafter in accordance with the 
supervised person’s level of parole supervision.  
(f) When the Containment Team makes a determination to retain a participant in a sex 
offender management program, the determination shall be supported by good cause, as 
defined in Section 3000. A determination to retain a supervised person in a sex offender 
management program shall be stated in writing, signed by the sex offender treatment 
provider and parole agent on the CDCR Form 3043 Containment Team Meeting / Earned 
Discharge Consideration Committee (Rev.711/24), which is incorporated by reference. 
This completed form shall be delivered to the supervised person within 30 calendar days 
of the CTM and maintained in the supervised person’s file. Reasons to retain a supervised 
person in a sex offender management program may include, but are not limited to: 
(1) Pursuant to Section 3573, a Level of Service or Case Management Inventory (LS/CMI) 
score of 11 or higher. 
 
(2) Pursuant to Section 3573, a Stable-2007 score of four or higher for males only. 
 
(3) A current polygraph completed with deception found or new disclosure admissions 
that the supervised person has committed acts that would incur a technical or law 
violation. 
 
(4) Parole violation(s), relevant to the supervised person’s sex offense or adherence to 
the Conditions and Special Conditions of Parole associated with their sex offense, that 
occurred within one year of the review. 
 
(g) The parole agent and unit supervisor may re-refer a supervised person to a sex 
offender management program for evaluation if there is a change in the supervised 
person’s behaviors related to the risk of re-offense to a level likely to lead to a risk to

public safety, using the CDCR 1502 (Rev. 07/24) Activity Report. A re-referral may also 
be initiated at the request of the supervised person.  
 
(1) Upon re-referral, the sex offender treatment provider shall complete the dynamic risk 
and violence risk assessments, pursuant to section 3573 and PC sections 290.04 and 
290.09, to determine if the risk to re-offend has increased. 
 
(A) If risk to re-offend has increased, the supervised person will be required to attend the 
sex offender management program, with the prescribed hours of treatment being 
determined by the sex offender treatment provider, until the increased risk to re-offend 
has been mitigated. While the supervised person is attending a sex offender management 
program, CTMs shall be re-established in accordance with Section 3574.  
 
(B) If the sex offender treatment provider determines there is no increased risk in re-
offense, the re-referral shall be considered closed, and the sex offender management 
program requirements remain completed.

On January 3, 2025, the California Department of Corrections and Rehabilitation  
(CDCR or the department) published the Notice of Change to Regulations for Sex 
Offender Treatment, which began the public comment period. The department’s Notice 
of Change to Regulations 25-01 was mailed the same day to individuals who had 
requested to be on the department’s mailing list for regulation changes, was posted on 
the department’s website, and copies were posted in CDCR institutions. Five written 
public comments were received during the public comment period. The comments are 
summarized and responded to below under the heading Summaries and Responses to 
Written Public Comments Received During the Initial Comment Period. A public hearing 
was held on February 20, 2025. The department received no comments during the public 
hearing.  
DETER0INATIONS, ASSESS0ENTS, 0ANDATES, AND FISCAL I0PACT  
The department has determined that no alternative considered would be more effective 
in carrying out the purpose for which this regulation is proposed or would be as effective 
and less burdensome to affected private persons or would be more cost effective to 
affected private persons and equally effective in implementing the statutory policy or other 
provision of law than the action proposed. No such alternatives were proposed or brought 
to the department’s attention during the adoption of this rulemaking action.  
The department has made an initial determination that the action will not have a significant 
adverse economic impact on business. Additionally, there has been no testimony or other 
evidence provided that would alter the department’s initial determination.  
The department has determined that this action imposes no mandates on local agencies 
or school districts, or a mandate which requires reimbursement pursuant to Part 7 
(Section 1751) of Division 4 of the *overnment Code (*C).  
The department has determined that no reasonable alternatives to the regulation have 
been identified or brought to the attention of the department that would lessen any 
adverse impact on affected private persons or small businesses than the action planned.  
The department, in proposing the adoption of these regulations, has not identified nor has 
it relied upon any technical, theoretical, or empirical study, report, or similar document.  
The department has relied upon the results of the Economic Impact Assessment, which 
can be found in the Notice of Proposed Regulations and is available for review as part of 
the rulemaking file.

Commenter 1  
 
Comment 1 Pursuant to Section 3573, a Stable-2007 score of four or higher for males 
only shall be, amended to include but not limited to Transgender Men and Transgender 
Women.  In addition, to include any sexual predator who is a biological person whose 
identity includes not soley Male or Transgender Female, or nonbinary.  A stable score 
shall also be applicable to former biological males that now identify with an identity other 
than male.    
 
In addition, it is imperative that the Aftercare Phase is a Mandatory Outpatient phase in 
the format of a support group with the sex offender treatment provider. The phase shall 
be for supervised persons and shall be mandated for no less than one, continuous year, 
to continue the sex offender
s participation in the sex offender management program after 
the sex offender has successfully completed the curriculum and maintenance phases, or 
persons who have been discharged from parole supervision. 
 
Response 1  
 
California Code of Regulations (CCR), Title 15, Section 3574 Sex Offender Treatment (f) 
(2) references reasons to retain a supervised person in a sex offender management 
program. Pursuant to this section, a Stable-2007 score of four or higher for males only is 
a factor. The California Sex Offender Management Board (CASOMB) has established 
State Authorized Risk Assessment Tools for Sex Offenders (SARATSO). These 
assessments are validated, and sex offender management professionals utilize the 
appropriate coding manual and addendums for determining scoring. The Stable-2007 is 
for males only and utilizes the appropriate coding. *ender identity is not a factor in the 
validation or application of the tool.  
 
Regarding part two of the comment, CCR Title 15, Section 3574, Sex Offender Treatment, 
provides for a comprehensive evaluation of risk and needs for each supervised person. 
Sex Offender Treatment (SOT) participation is based on risk of re-offense to a level likely 
to lead to a risk to public safety. When the supervised person has successfully completed 
the maintenance phase it has been determined that their risk and needs have decreased 

Final Statement of Reasons NCR 25-01 
4/17/25 
3 
sufficiently to complete treatment. Additionally, requiring a person to attend a phase of 
treatment after it has been determined that they have successfully completed contradicts 
the purpose of the regulation. Lastly, aftercare phase is also voluntarily, attended by those 
who have discharged parole. The Division of Adult Parole Operations (DAPO) does not 
have the authority to require a person attend treatment if that person is no longer under 
the jurisdiction of DAPO. 
 
Commenter   
 
Comment Commenter is an incarcerated person from +igh Desert State Prison. 
Commenter wants to know if there is a part from the proposed regulations for incarcerated 
persons who plead ³no contest.´ Commenter states these people were accused of 
horrible charges and had no choice but to accept deals. Commenter states these groups 
should be able to live their life without watching their backs. These incarcerated persons 
should be reviewed on a case-by-case basis, including review of the programs complete 
while incarcerated, and the evidence for the crime accused of, upon their release. 
 
Response   
 
The requirement for persons placed on parole, that are required to register pursuant to 
Penal Code (PC) sections 290 to 290.023, inclusive, attend sex offender treatment as 
required by PC 3008(d). Specifically, PC 3008(d)(2) states, ³Persons placed on parole on 
or after July 1, 2012, shall successfully complete a sex offender management program, 
following the standards developed pursuant to Section 9003, as a condition of parole. The 
length of the period in the program shall be not less than one year, up to the entire period 
of parole, as determined by the certified sex offender management professional in 
consultation with the parole officer and as approved by the court. Participation in this 
program applies to every person described without regard to when his or her crime or 
crimes were committed.´ 
 
These regulations only establish parameters for the existing PC and are unable to alter 
the existing requirements set forth by PC. 
 
Commenter 3  
 
Comment 3 Commenter is an incarcerated person who provides some background 
information to their incarceration and sentencing. Commenter states that there are no 
rehabilitation efforts for incarcerated persons who are sentences as sex offenders, only 
punitive efforts. Commenter provides support for the proposed sex offender treatment 
program, but states that sex offender treatment efforts should be offered before release 
and completed during incarceration not after release, due to different life circumstances 
after release.  
 
Response 3

These regulations only establish parameters for the existing PC and are unable to alter 
the existing requirements set forth by PC. DAPO must abide by PC 3008(d)(2), which 
states, ³Persons placed on parole on or after July 1, 2012, shall successfully complete a 
sex offender management program, following the standards developed pursuant to 
Section 9003, as a condition of parole. The length of the period in the program shall be 
not less than one year, up to the entire period of parole, as determined by the certified 
sex offender management professional in consultation with the parole officer and as 
approved by the court. Participation in this program applies to every person described 
without regard to when his or her crime or crimes were committed.´ 
 
Additionally, the proposed regulations are regarding Sex Offender Treatment after the 
release from incarceration. The proposed regulations do not address institutional sex 
offender treatment programs or their availability. Therefore, the department cannot speak 
to or address this subject matter at the moment. 
 
Lastly, your comment identifies concerns for potential costs associated with a supervised 
person’s request for a voluntary re-referral to SOT. PC 3008(e) states, ³Any defendant 
ordered to be placed in an approved sex offender management treatment program 
pursuant to subdivision (d) shall be responsible for paying the expense of their 
participation in the program. The department shall take into consideration the ability of 
the defendant to pay, and no defendant shall be denied discharge onto parole because 
of their inability to pay.´

Comments 4 and 5 are duplicative Commenter is a sex offender treatment provider 
and is responding to NCR 25-05 to solicitate their services and be considered as a

Response 4 The comment is either insufficiently related to the specific action or actions 
proposed, or too generalized or personalized to the extent that no meaningful response 
can be formulated by the department in refutation of or accommodation to the comment. 
Therefore, the comment is being dismissed.

Superior Court of the State of California
COUNTY OF ALAMEDA


Petitioner Brendan Ngehsi Newanforbi (“Petitioner”) and Respondents Gerardo Serrato (“Capt. Serrato”), Gary Paul (“Lt. Paul”), Eric Dutra (“Sgt. Dutra”) (collectively, “Individual Respondents”), by and through their respective counsel, hereby stipulate as follows:
RECITALS
Petitioner filed his Petition for Writ of Mandate against Respondents California Highway Patrol (“CHP”), Gerardo Serrato, Gary Paul, and Eric Dutra in this action on May 29, 2026.
The Individual Respondents were served with the Petition for Writ of Mandate on June 30, 2026.
On July 10, Respondent CHP filed its Demurrer to the Petition for Writ of Mandate.  Respondent CHP reserved a hearing date of August 28, 2026.
On July 27, 2026, counsel for the Individual Respondents reserved hearing dates of October 16, 2026 and October 23, 2026 for the Individual Respondents’ intended Demurrers and Joinders to CHP’s Demurrer. 
On July 27, 2026, during a telephonic meet-and-confer, counsel for Petitioner and the Individual Respondents agreed to stipulate to advance the October 16 and October 23 hearing dates to August 28, 2026, to be heard at the same time as CHP’s Demurrer.  Communications reflecting that agreement were exchanged between counsel.  
On July 30, 2026, the Individual Respondents filed their Demurrers and Joinders to Respondent California Highway Patrol’s Demurrer to the Petition for Writ of Mandate.  
STIPULATION
The parties respectfully request and HEREBY STIPULATE as follows:
The October 16 and October 23 hearings on the Individual Respondents’ Demurrers and Joinders to CHP’s Demurrer shall be advanced to August 28, 2026, at 9:00 a.m., to be heard at the same time as CHP’s Demurrer.
IT IS SO STIPULATED. 
[Signature Page Immediately Follows]

After full consideration of the Parties’ Joint Stipulation to Advance Dates of Hearings on Demurrers of Individual Respondents, the Court HEREBY ORDERS as follows:  
IT IS ORDERED that the hearings on the Demurrers and Joinders of Respondents Gerardo Serrato, Gary Paul, and Eric Dutra be advanced to August 28, 2026 at 9:00 a.m.
IT IS SO ORDERED.

CONFIDENTIAL SETTLEMENT AGREEMENT AND RELEASE
This Confidential Settlement and Release Agreement (Agreement) is entered into between 
Brendan Ngwa Nforbi, also known as Brendan Ngehsi Newanforbi (you) and Pilot Travel 
Centers LLC (Company). You and the Company (together, the Parties) agree as follows:
•
Termination of Employment Relationship: Your employment relationship with the 
Company ended in January 2026.
•
Representations: You represent that you have reported all work-related injuries, if any, 
to the Company prior to the time of your termination.
•
Consideration: In return for your promises in this Agreement, and provided that you 
sign and return this Agreement the Company will pay you the gross amount of 
$35,000.00, inclusive of attorneys’ fees and costs with respect to the released claims, 
within fifteen business days after the effective date, and provided that the required W-4 
and W-9 forms are returned with this signed Agreement, allocated and payable as 
follows:
•
One check payable to Brendan Ngwa Nforbi for alleged wage-based damages, in the 
gross amount of $10,000.00 less applicable taxes and other authorized or required 
withholdings, for which an IRS Form W-2 will be issued to you;
•
One check payable to Brendan Ngwa Nforbi, for alleged non-wage compensatory 
damages, in the amount of $25,000.00** **for which an IRS Form 1099 will be issued to 
you This Agreement is not intended, nor does it purport to give you advice or counseling 
concerning federal, state, or local tax responsibilities or liabilities. You acknowledge this 
payment is in addition to anything you would have received had you not signed this 
Agreement. Amounts the Company is paying in consideration for the Agreement will be 
treated as taxable compensation but are not intended by either party to be treated, and 
will not be treated, as compensation for purposes of eligibility or benefits under any 
benefit plan of the Company.
•
You must provide required tax documentation, including a W-4 for you and a W-9 for 
you.
All checks will be mailed overnight to you at 1455 Cat Tail Drive, Stockton, CA 95204.
•
Indemnification: You shall be solely responsible for the payment of any federal, state, or 
local taxes arising out of the payment of non-wage monies under the Agreement. You 
agree to hold the Company harmless from any and all claims, demands, rights, damages, 
costs or expenses resulting from any liability or claim of liability for any amount 
assessed by or due any federal, state, or local government or agency thereof, including 
but not limited to federal, state, and local withholding and income taxes and social 
security taxes, with respect to payments made by the Company to you as set out in this 
Agreement.
•
Full and Final Release: In exchange for the benefits provided by the Company under this 
Agreement, you fully and forever release and discharge the Company, its parents, 
1 of 6

subsidiaries, affiliates, and related entities and all of their respective agents, attorneys, 
employees, officers, directors, shareholders, members, managers, employee benefit 
plans and fiduciaries, insurers, successors, and assigns, (Released Parties) from any and 
all claims and potential claims that may legally be waived by private agreement, 
whether known or unknown, which you have asserted or could assert against the 
Company arising out of or relating in any way to any acts, circumstances, facts, 
transactions, omissions, based on facts occurring up to and including the date you sign 
this Agreement (Claims). You understand that you are releasing such Claims on behalf 
of yourself and all persons who could make Claims under, through or by you, such as 
your spouse, heirs, executors or assignees.
This release includes, but is not limited to, (i) any and all claims under the California Labor 
Code, the Fair Employment and Housing Act, California Penal Code Section 290.46(j), any and 
all Claims arising under Title VII of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, the Civil Rights Act of 1866, the 
Civil Rights Act of 1991, the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), the Employee Retirement 
Income Security Act (ERISA), the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA), the Americans with 
Disabilities Act (ADA), any amendments to such laws, any other federal, state, or local 
constitution, charter, law, rule, ordinance, regulation, or order or those of any other count; (ii) 
any individual claim for penalties under the Private Attorneys General Act; (iii) Claims in 
equity or under common law including claims for tort, breach of contract (express or implied, 
written or oral), wrongful discharge, defamation, emotional distress, and negligence; (iv) all 
Claims made or which could have been made in the Complaint filed in San Joaquin County 
Superior Court (Case No. STK-CV-UWT-2026-0007649).
Specifically excluded from this Agreement are any claims that cannot be released as a matter of 
law through a private agreement, for example a claim for unemployment insurance or workers’ 
compensation benefits.
You understand and agree that you are releasing all rights under section 1542 of the California 
Civil Code. Section 1542 provides as follows:
A GENERAL RELEASE DOES NOT EXTEND TO CLAIMS THAT THE CREDITOR OR RELEASING 
PARTY DOES NOT KNOW OR SUSPECT TO EXIST IN HIS OR HER FAVOR AT THE TIME OF 
EXECUTING THE RELEASE, AND THAT, IF KNOWN BY HIM OR HER, WOULD HAVE 
MATERIALLY AFFECTED HIS OR HER SETTLEMENT WITH THE DEBTOR OR RELEASED 
PARTY.
•
Attorneys’ Fees/Medicare and Medicaid Interest: This Agreement settles and releases 
any and all claims for attorneys’ fees with respect to the settled claims. This settlement 
is based upon a good faith determination of the Parties to resolve a disputed claim. The 
Parties have not shifted responsibility of medical treatment to Medicare or Medicaid in 
contravention of 42 U.S.C. §1395y(b). The Parties resolved this matter in compliance 
with both federal, state, and local law. The Parties made every effort to adequately 
protect the interests of Medicare and Medicaid.
•
Non-Admission: This Agreement shall not be construed as an admission by the 
Company of any liability or acts of wrongdoing or unlawful conduct, nor shall it be 
considered to be evidence of such liability, wrongdoing, or unlawful discrimination.

•
Dismissal of the Action. Within five (5) business days of receipt of the payments 
described in Paragraph 3, above, you shall file a Request for Dismissal in the Superior 
Court case in San Joaquin County, dismissing Case No. STK-CV-UWT-2026-0007649, as

•
Proprietary Information: To the extent you have any, you understand that you are

software, files, papers, memoranda, correspondence, customer lists, financial data, 
credit cards, keys, tape recordings, pictures, and security access cards, and any other 
items of any nature which are the property of the Company, regardless of whether you 
sign this Agreement. To the fullest extent permitted by law, you also agree to retain in 
confidence any confidential information known to you concerning the Company until 
such information is publicly available.
•
Confidentiality of Agreement: You agree that you will maintain the confidentiality of 
this Agreement and will not disclose in any fashion the nature and terms of this 
Agreement, the amount of this settlement, and/or the substance or content of

of the information (with the exception of a governmental agency), and such individuals

Non-Disparagement/Neutral Reference: You agree not to make statements to clients,

are in any way disparaging or negative towards the Released Parties or their products 
and services. The Company agrees that if it receives a request for an employment

Re:   Pre-Filing Demand for Settlement -- Newanforbi v. Pilot Travel Centers LLC
Unlawful Use of California Sex Offender Registry Information for Employment in
Violation of Cal. Penal Code § 290.46(j); Wrongful Termination; FCRA / ICRAA
Violations; Demand for $475,000.00 and Injunctive Relief
Pilot Employee ID: 573787   |   Checkr Report ID: 43f3d4df15540eaf0ba009f3   |   Adverse
Action Date: December 30, 2025
Dear Ms. Rigamonti:
I write, pro per, to demand pre-litigation settlement of the claims described herein arising from
Pilot Travel Centers LLC's ("Pilot" or the "Company") unlawful termination of my employment based
solely on my registration in the California Sex Offender Registry. Pilot's own written Post-Adverse
Action Notice of December 30, 2025 is an unqualified admission that the Company used Megan's Law
registry information to take adverse employment action against me -- the precise conduct that
California Penal Code section 290.46, subdivision (j)(2)(E), categorically prohibits.
A complete Draft Complaint for Damages, prepared for filing in the Superior Court of
California, County of San Joaquin, is enclosed as Exhibit A. The Draft Complaint asserts seven causes
of action, names Pilot Travel Centers LLC as the defendant, demands trial by jury, and is in final form.
I will file and serve the Complaint, together with a contemporaneous press release summarizing the
documentary record, on the deadline set forth in Section IX below absent a satisfactory settlement.

Pre-Filing Demand Letter -- Newanforbi v. Pilot Travel Centers LLC -- Page 2
CONFIDENTIAL SETTLEMENT COMMUNICATION -- Cal. Evid. Code Section 1152 / Fed. R. Evid. 408
I.   THE FACTS ARE DOCUMENTARY AND UNDISPUTED
This case will not turn on credibility. Every material fact is established by Pilot's own writings,
Pilot's own HR system entries, Pilot's own background-check vendor's report, and Pilot's own
post-adverse action notice. The complete documentary chain is in my possession and attached to the
Draft Complaint:
•   December 10, 2025:   Pilot, by its authorized representative Chris W. Kiley (Employee
No. 7005), extended me a written offer of employment for the position of Guest Services
Leader at $24.00/hour, with a $500 sign-on bonus, comprehensive benefits, and an
anticipated start date of December 15, 2025.
•   December 15, 2025:   Pilot issued Employee ID 573787, formally added me to its HR
system, assigned me to PTC Lodi, CA, Retail Travel Center 617, and welcomed me to "the
Pilot family." I commenced active employment.
•   Dec. 15, 2025 - Jan. 23, 2026:   I worked regular shifts at the Lodi Travel Center and
received five paychecks from Pilot totaling approximately $2,673.02 in gross wages, each
posted to my Valley Strong Credit Union account as "Salary/Regular Income from Pilot
Flying J."
•   December 23, 2025:   Checkr, Inc., Pilot's background check vendor, completed Report
ID 43f3d4df15540eaf0ba009f3. The report returned a status of "Consider" -- not
disqualifying. Every county criminal search (San Joaquin, CA; Washoe, NV; Santa Clara,
CA; Sheridan, WY) returned "Clear." The Global Watchlist returned "Clear." The only
flag was a single entry in the CA Sex Offender Registry.
• 
 
 
December 
30, 
2025, 
5:10 
p.m.: 
 
 
Pilot, 
through 
its
backgroundcheck@pilottravelcenters.com address, sent me a "Post-adverse action notice"
terminating me. The notice identified the basis for the adverse action as one single item:
“REGISTRATION IN CA SEX OFFENDER REGISTRY”
Pilot's notice did not identify any criminal conviction. Did not identify any court record. Did not
allege any job-related safety concern. Did not invoke the "protect a person at risk" exception. Cited one
item, in capital letters, and one item only.
II.   THE LAW IS UNAMBIGUOUS
California Penal Code section 290.46, subdivision (j), provides in pertinent part:
“(1) A person is authorized to use information disclosed pursuant to this section only
to protect a person at risk.
(2) Except as authorized under paragraph (1) or any other provision of law, use of any
information that is disclosed pursuant to this section for purposes relating to ... (E)
Employment ... is prohibited.”
The statute is categorical. It is not a balancing test. It is not a "consider all factors" provision. It
contains exactly one narrow exception -- the "protect a person at risk" exception -- which by its terms
requires an identified individual exposed to a specific risk of a sex offense in the context of the
particular job. A retail travel-center cashier position does not qualify, and Pilot's adverse action notice

Pre-Filing Demand Letter -- Newanforbi v. Pilot Travel Centers LLC -- Page 3
CONFIDENTIAL SETTLEMENT COMMUNICATION -- Cal. Evid. Code Section 1152 / Fed. R. Evid. 408
does not even purport to invoke the exception.
Pilot's own consumer-reporting vendor, Checkr, included the mandatory California statutory
disclaimer directly on the face of the report. Pilot was warned, in writing, by its own vendor, of the
very statute the Company proceeded to violate.
III.   THE STATUTORY REMEDIES ARE EXTRAORDINARY
Penal Code section 290.46 imposes uniquely punitive consequences for the violation Pilot has
committed:
•   Treble actual damages.   § 290.46(l) -- every dollar of lost wages, lost benefits, and
consequential economic harm is multiplied by three.
•   Civil penalty of $10,000 to $25,000 per violation.   § 290.46(k) -- a separate, statutory
penalty independent of actual damages.
•   Mandatory attorney fees and costs.   § 290.46(l) -- recoverable by the prevailing
plaintiff as a matter of right.
•   Wrongful termination tort damages.   Common-law Tameny claim: compensatory
damages, non-economic damages, and punitive damages on a willful, oppressive, malicious
violation.
•   FCRA statutory and punitive damages.   15 U.S.C. §§ 1681n, 1681o -- $100 to $1,000
per violation, plus punitive damages and attorney fees on a willful violation.
•   ICRAA actual and punitive damages.   Cal. Civ. Code § 1786.50 -- with attorney fees.
•   UCL injunctive relief and restitution.   Cal. Bus. & Prof. Code § 17200 -- including a
court order requiring Pilot to cease this practice statewide.
IV.   THE DAMAGES MODEL

The damages model above does not account for the FCRA statutory damages on a per-violation
basis, the ICRAA punitive exposure, the UCL restitution claim, prejudgment interest, costs, or the
mandatory attorney fee award -- all of which add further to Pilot's exposure.
V.   WHY SETTLEMENT NOW IS IN PILOT'S INTEREST
Beyond the raw damages exposure, three additional factors counsel pre-filing resolution:
1.   The smoking gun is in your file, not mine. The Post-Adverse Action Notice was generated by
Pilot's own background-check department on Pilot's own letterhead, sent from a Pilot email address.
There is no theory under which Pilot did not use registry information for employment. The document
says it did. Discovery will only make this worse for the Company, not better.
2.   The case will create public precedent. California Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E) is rarely litigated
in the employment context precisely because most employers know not to put the violation in writing.
Pilot did. A published verdict or opinion in Newanforbi v. Pilot becomes permanent training material
for every plaintiffs' employment lawyer in California, with Pilot's name on it.
3.   The collateral exposure is institutional. If Pilot uses this same Checkr-driven process at any of its
other California locations -- and a corporate background-check department generally does -- the UCL
injunctive-relief count, the discovery into Pilot's nationwide adverse-action data, and the possibility of
class certification all transform this from a single-plaintiff case into a multi-million-dollar institutional
risk. Pre-filing resolution eliminates that risk.
VI.   THE DEMAND
To resolve all claims arising out of the matters described herein without litigation, I demand the
following:
SETTLEMENT PAYMENT: $475,000.00
(Four Hundred Seventy-Five Thousand U.S. Dollars)
Payable by check to: BRENDAN NGWA NFORBI
Plus the following non-monetary terms, each of which is material to settlement:
    (a) Internal policy correction. Written confirmation, signed by an officer of Pilot, that the
Company has issued binding written guidance to its background-check department, HR, and recruiting
personnel in California that California Sex Offender Registry information shall not be used as the basis
for any employment action.

    (b) Removal from internal records. Confirmation that all references to the December 30, 2025
adverse action have been expunged from my employment file, including in the Click Boarding and
PILOT_PRD_HCM systems, and that my separation has been recoded as eligible for rehire.
    (c) Neutral reference. A written commitment that all future employer inquiries regarding my
employment at Pilot will be answered with dates of employment, position held, and "eligible for rehire"
only.
    (d) Withdrawal of the December 30, 2025 notice. Written withdrawal of the Post-Adverse Action
Notice, signed by the Chief Legal Officer or designee.
    (e) Confidentiality of settlement amount only. The fact of settlement and the non-monetary terms
may be disclosed; only the dollar amount will be confidential. I will not agree to a non-disparagement
clause or any release broader than the claims arising from the December 30, 2025 adverse action.
    (f) No re-tender of employment required. Settlement is in lieu of reinstatement.
VII.   FORMAL LITIGATION HOLD NOTICE
This letter operates as formal notice of Pilot's duty to preserve evidence under Cedars-Sinai
Medical Center v. Superior Court (1998) 18 Cal.4th 1, and applicable federal authorities. Pilot is
directed to immediately suspend any auto-deletion, archive-purge, or document-retention policies that
would result in the destruction, alteration, or loss of any of the following:
•   All documents, e-mails, system entries, and communications concerning my
application(s), recruitment, offer, hire, onboarding, employment, background check, adverse
action, and separation, including but not limited to the Click Boarding system, the
PILOT_PRD_HCM HR system, the SmartRecruiters platform, the Checkr candidate portal,
the backgroundcheck@pilottravelcenters.com mailbox, and all related backup tapes,
archives, and audit logs;
•   All policies, procedures, training materials, scripts, decision rubrics, automated
workflows, and adjudication matrices used by Pilot's background-check department for
California candidates, in effect at any time between January 1, 2024 and the present;
•   All communications between Pilot and Checkr, Inc. concerning California candidates
flagged with sex offender registry hits;
•   All data identifying every California candidate or employee against whom Pilot took
adverse action between January 1, 2024 and the present based, in whole or in part, on sex
offender registry information.
Failure to preserve will be the subject of a CCP § 2023.030 spoliation motion and a request for
adverse-inference instruction at trial.
VIII.   SETTLEMENT-COMMUNICATION PROTECTION
This letter is offered in compromise of a disputed claim and is inadmissible to prove liability
under California Evidence Code section 1152 and Federal Rule of Evidence 408. The factual recitations
are based on Pilot's own documentary record; nothing in this letter limits my right to introduce the
underlying documents as evidence at trial.

IX.   DEADLINE FOR RESPONSE
Pilot must respond in writing or by email to bnn.cdl@gmail.com, on or before 5:00 p.m. Pacific
Time on June 15, 2026. Absent a written or e-mail acceptance of these terms, or a good-faith
counter-offer, by that deadline, the enclosed Draft Complaint will be filed in the San Joaquin County
Superior Court without further notice.
I am willing to participate in a single, good-faith mediation session within the deadline window if
Pilot's counsel believes it would expedite resolution. I am not willing to extend the deadline absent that
commitment.
X.   RESERVATION OF RIGHTS
Nothing in this letter waives, releases, or limits any claim, right, or remedy. All claims, rights, and
remedies are expressly reserved. This letter is not, and shall not be construed as, an offer to settle for
any amount less than that stated herein, nor as an admission of fact, law, or comparative fault.
I look forward to your prompt response.

NATURE OF THE ACTION
1. This is an action for damages arising from Defendant's willful, knowing, and unlawful
use of California Megan's Law Sex Offender Registry information to terminate Plaintiff's
employment, in direct and express violation of California Penal Code section 290.46, subdivision
(j)(2)(E), which categorically prohibits the use of sex offender registry information for any
employment purpose.
2. On December 10, 2025, Defendant extended Plaintiff a written offer of employment for
the position of Guest Services Leader at Defendant's Lodi, California Travel Center (Store No.
617), at a starting hourly rate of $24.00, with a $500 sign-on bonus after ninety days, and
comprehensive benefits. Plaintiff accepted the offer.
3. On December 15, 2025, Defendant assigned Plaintiff Employee ID 573787 in
Defendant's HR system, completed Plaintiff's onboarding, and Plaintiff commenced active
employment at the Lodi Travel Center. Plaintiff worked regular shifts and received weekly
paychecks from Defendant through the pay periods ending in mid-January 2026.
4. On December 30, 2025, while Plaintiff was a current, active employee, Defendant
issued a "Post-adverse action notice" to Plaintiff by email from
backgroundcheck@pilottravelcenters.com, stating that Plaintiff's background report "does not
meet Pilot Travel Centers LLC (the 'Company') standards" and that the decision was based on a
single item: "REGISTRATION IN CA SEX OFFENDER REGISTRY."
5. Defendant's own adverse action notice expressly identifies the California Sex Offender
Registry as the sole basis for the employment action. California Penal Code section 290.46,
subdivision (j)(2)(E), enacted as part of the Megan's Law public-notification framework,
unambiguously provides that the use of registry information disclosed under that section "for

10. Plaintiff BRENDAN NGEHSI NEWANFORBI (also known of record as Brendan
Ngwa Nforbi) is a natural person and resident of Stockton, San Joaquin County, California.
Plaintiff was employed by Defendant as a Guest Services Leader at Defendant's Lodi, California
Travel Center from on or about December 15, 2025 until his termination on or about January
2026, arising from the unlawful adverse action notice dated December 30, 2025.
11. Defendant PILOT TRAVEL CENTERS LLC is a Delaware limited liability company
doing business as "Pilot Flying J" and "Pilot Company," with its principal place of business in
Knoxville, Tennessee, and operating numerous retail travel center locations throughout
California, including PTC Lodi, CA, Retail Travel Center 617, located in San Joaquin County,
California. Defendant is an "employer" within the meaning of all applicable employment statutes.
STATUTORY AND LEGAL FRAMEWORK
A. California Penal Code Section 290.46 -- Megan's Law Registry Protections
12. California Penal Code section 290.46 governs the public disclosure and permitted use
of sex offender registry information under the Megan's Law framework. Subdivision (j)(1)
provides that a person is authorized to use information disclosed pursuant to the section only to
protect a person at risk. Subdivision (j)(2) then provides that, except as authorized under
paragraph (1) or any other provision of law, use of any information disclosed pursuant to the
section for purposes relating to specified categories -- including, at subdivision (j)(2)(E), 
"Employment" -- is prohibited.
13. The statutory prohibition is categorical and absolute for employment purposes. The
Legislature deliberately prohibited the use of registry information for employment decisions to
prevent precisely the kind of automatic disqualification that Defendant engaged in here. The only

narrow exception -- using information "to protect a person at risk" under subdivision (j)(1) --
applies only where a specific, identified person is or may be exposed to a risk of becoming a
victim of a sex offense by the registrant in the specific context of that job.
14. Remedies. Penal Code section 290.46, subdivision (k), provides that any person who
uses information disclosed pursuant to the section in violation of the section shall be subject to a
civil penalty of not less than ten thousand dollars ($10,000) and not more than twenty-five
thousand dollars ($25,000) for each violation. Subdivision (l) further provides that any person
who is harmed by a violation of the section may bring a civil action for damages, including treble
actual damages, costs, and reasonable attorney fees.
B. The Fair Credit Reporting Act (15 U.S.C. Section 1681 et seq.)
15. The federal Fair Credit Reporting Act ("FCRA") imposes specific duties on employers
who use "consumer reports" for employment purposes. Under 15 U.S.C. section 1681b(b)(3),
before taking adverse action based in whole or in part on a consumer report, an employer must:
(a) provide the consumer a copy of the report; and (b) provide the consumer a written description
of the consumer's rights under the Act. An employer who willfully fails to comply with these
requirements is liable for actual damages or statutory damages of not less than $100 and not more
than $1,000 per violation, punitive damages, and reasonable attorney fees. (15 U.S.C. sections
1681n, 1681o.)
16. An adverse employment action that is based on information the employer is legally
prohibited from considering is not a permissible purpose under FCRA, and an employer that
relies on such prohibited information acts willfully within the meaning of section 1681n.
C. California Investigative Consumer Reporting Agencies Act (Civ. Code Section 1786 et seq.)

17. The California Investigative Consumer Reporting Agencies Act ("ICRAA") regulates
the preparation and use of investigative consumer reports in California. Under Civil Code section
1786.50, any person who willfully fails to comply with the ICRAA is liable for actual damages,
punitive damages, and reasonable attorney fees. Any person who negligently fails to comply is
liable for actual damages and reasonable attorney fees.
D. California Unfair Competition Law (Bus. & Prof. Code Section 17200 et seq.)
18. California's Unfair Competition Law ("UCL") prohibits any unlawful, unfair, or
fraudulent business act or practice. An employment practice that violates Penal Code section
290.46(j) constitutes an "unlawful" business practice under the UCL. The UCL provides for
restitution and injunctive relief.
E. Wrongful Termination in Violation of Public Policy
19. Under California common law, an employer may not discharge an employee for a
reason that contravenes fundamental public policy. (Tameny v. Atlantic Richfield Co. (1980) 27
Cal.3d 167.) A termination that violates a statute designed to protect a class of persons constitutes
a wrongful termination in violation of public policy. The public policy embodied in Penal Code
section 290.46(j) -- prohibiting the use of registry information for employment -- is tethered to a
statute, is fundamental, is beneficial to the public, and was clearly established at the time of
Defendant's conduct. A Tameny claim entitles the plaintiff to compensatory damages, including
economic and non-economic damages, and punitive damages where the defendant's conduct is
shown to be willful, oppressive, or malicious.

hundreds of locations across California with a dedicated background check department

56. Plaintiff incorporates by reference paragraphs 1 through 47 as though fully set forth
herein.
57. Penal Code section 290.46(j)(2)(E) embodies a fundamental public policy of the State
of California: that employers shall not use Megan's Law sex offender registry information to
make employment decisions. This public policy is (a) delineated in a constitutional or statutory
provision; (b) fundamental; (c) beneficial to the public as a whole, not merely to the individual;
and (d) well-established at the time of Defendant's conduct.
58. Defendant terminated Plaintiff's employment in contravention of this fundamental
public policy by basing the termination on Plaintiff's registration in the California Sex Offender

12/10/2025
Brendan Ngwa Nforbi
bnn.cdl@gmail.com
Dear Brendan:
Welcome to the Pilot family! We are pleased to extend to you a contingent offer of employment for the position of 
Guest Services Leader with an anticipated start date of 12/15/2025. This offer is contingent upon receipt of a 
satisfactory background check and rehire eligibility, if applicable. 
The terms of the offer are as follows:
Your starting base Hourly compensation will be $USD 24.00, payable as earned on a weekly basis. If overtime eligible, 
your overtime pay will be calculated in accordance with federal, state and local requirements.

You will not be eligible to receive a merit increase until the next performance cycle.

In order for any Bonus payment to be considered earned and payable, you must be actively employed and in 
good standing with PILOT at the time payment is issued.

You will receive a one-time Gross Sign-On bonus of $USD 500.00 after 90 days from the start date of this role.

Health, Dental, and Vision: Benefits are effective on the earlier of: (1) the 1st day of the month following or 
coincident with the 30th day of service (where the date of hire is treated as day 1); or (2) if the date of hire is the 
first day of a calendar month, then the 1st day of the second calendar month beginning after the date of hire. 
You should enroll in your chosen benefits as soon as you receive a benefits postcard in the mail, approximately 
two weeks after your hire date. You must enroll in your selected benefits prior to the day that you first become 
eligible to receive them.

Information regarding Paid Time Off (PTO), Parental Leave, Life Insurance, and other special benefits are 
included in the Benefits Guidebook or PILOTco; eligibility and effective dates can differ by benefit program.

401(k) plan: All Team Members who are at least 18 are eligible to participate in the 401(k) plan immediately 
upon hire. Principal, Pilot’s 401(k) provider, will mail out information about the plan to your home address. 
About two weeks after your hire date, you will be able to create an account at Principal.com to make your 
contribution election to begin contributing. Pilot does not automatically enroll participants, so you must make 
an affirmative election. If you are participating, company matching contributions will begin 1 year after your 
original hire date and will be immediately vested. Pilot matches 100% of the first 3% you contribute, and 50% of 
the next 2% you contribute.
Pilot shall have the right to withhold from any amount payable hereunder any federal, state, and local taxes in order for 
Pilot to satisfy any withholding tax obligation it may have in respect to any applicable law or regulation.
This is an offer letter only and not an employment contract.  Your employment with Pilot is "at will," that is, it can be 
terminated with or without cause, at any time by Pilot or by you.  Accordingly, this offer does not constitute a guarantee 
of employment for a specified time period, but rather is an expression of Pilot’s good faith intent to offer you 
employment subject to the terms and conditions detailed above.  While employed at Pilot, you will be expected to 

follow any and all company policies and procedures and may be required as part of your onboarding to sign any 
acknowledgements of these policies and procedures, as well as any additional agreements as they relate to your 
position, compensation, and/or benefits.
Contact me if you have questions or need additional information.
Sincerely,
Kiley, Chris W. (7005)

bnn.cdl@gmail.com
Brendan - Congratulations on your job offer!
This letter has important and helpful information about your job offer.  
Please print or save it for your records and reference. 
What's Next?
Please review the details of your job offer and the next steps outlined below, then select 
"Accept" or "Decline" at the bottom of this page. 
OFFER DETAILS
Below are the details of your offer:
COMPANY: Macy's
JOB OFFER FOR: Captain, Selling and Support
POSITION APPLIED TO: Selling and Support Captain, Stockton Sherwood - Full Time
LOCATION: Macy's - Stockton Sherwood
ADDRESS: 5242 Pacific Ave, MCE 71338, Stockton, CA 95207, San Joaquin, United 
States
PAY RATE: $21.5 per hour. You will be paid for onboarding and training.
START DATE: May 28, 2026
During onboarding, you will receive schedule details for this position. You'll also learn how to 
use scheduling tools to expand your availability, enter days off, as well as pick up and switch 
shifts.
All offers are conditional upon successful completion of pre-employment screening, including 
rehire eligibility, prior contact with internal security, and where applicable, criminal history 
screening. 
*The entity that will employ you is not Macy's, Inc. but an affiliate, subsidiary or division of Macy'
s, Inc. Please note during your employment you may receive information that contains the logo 

Page | 2 of 3
or title Macy's, Inc. This does not change the identity of your employer but simply notes that this
information may be provided to one or more affiliates, subsidiaries and/or divisions in the Macy'
s organization.
NEXT STEPS
You will receive up to three VERY IMPORTANT emails shortly. If you don't see these emails, you might need 
to rescue them from your Spam folder.
•
First will be a request for additional information to finish accepting your job offer from 
jobs@macysbluemercurybloomingdalesjobs.com. 
•
Look for another email from HireRight about the background check.  
•
Once you've provided the necessary information, you'll get an email with your employee ID number and
password instructions from DBaasAdmin@macys.com.
Also, expect to receive a phone call from the store team in the next few days! 
YOUR FIRST DAY
What to Bring
Documentation: Federal law requires us to verify that all new hires are 
authorized to work in the United States by completing Form I-9. (In some 
states we also use E-Verify.) Refer to this list of Form I-9 Acceptable 
Documents, which lists the various documents you may use to establish 
identity and employment authorization. Please review this information and 
bring your choice of original Form I-9 documentation with you to onboarding. 
Be sure to provide the required documentation promptly, or we won't be able
to complete your employment.
Direct Deposit: The easiest and fastest way to receive your paycheck is to 
have it deposited directly into your bank account. Bring your bank account 
and routing number with you on your first day so you can designate where to
deposit your pay.  You can find your account and routing number on your 
personal check or in your banking app.  If you need help finding your 
account and routing number, please contact your banking institution prior to 
your first day. You may also choose the Skylight Program to access your full 
pay with no bank account - and no fees. The Skylight Program also gives 
you access to Skylight Network Checks. You can request a Skylight card in 
the location on your first day.
What to Wear
At Macy's, Inc. we always want to make a great impression on our 
customers. Please dress appropriately in professional attire for your first day.
You can view our dress code for Macy's by clicking this link. 

Page | 3 of 3
Background Check: This offer may be contingent on the satisfactory completion of all post-offer, pre-
employment screening, including criminal history screening, before beginning employment. Should there be an
unreasonable delay in receiving the results of your criminal history screening, the Company may allow you to 
begin employment pending the results of the screening. Please note, however, that if this occurs, the Company
reserves the right to end your employment should the results of the criminal history screening, once received, 
be deemed job-related following an appropriate review. 
PERKS
Total Rewards don't stop at your paycheck. There are many perks to working at Macy's, Inc. - including our 
colleague discount! On your first day, you will receive the opportunity to apply for a Credit Card or a Pre-Pay 
card which will allow you to receive up to a 20% discount on clothing, accessories, furniture, and most 
cosmetics. (Did someone say shopping spree?) Some hourly colleagues* are eligible for a team incentive. Talk
to your People Leader for details and eligibility. Finally, since we know you're going to love it here, we also 
offer a referral bonus* so you can refer friends and family to earn unlimited extra cash. *eligibility at affiliated 
locations may vary
On behalf of our entire team, congratulations!

reconciled with the contemporaneous recording.

19. The fabricated report was submitted to a magistrate to obtain Search Warrant No. 
11 
WAR913372 (approved by Judge A. Sekany at approximately 0234 hours, November 2, 2024). 
12 
At approximately 0238 hours, phlebotomist Aziza Ghaleb extracted two vials of blood from 
13 
Plaintiffs right arm at the CHP Dublin Area Office pursuant to the fraudulently obtained warrant. 
14 
15 
20. CHP conceded the arrest was unlawful. On or about November 5, 2024, CHP issued a 
16 
Detention Certificate under Penal Code section 851.6 reclassifying the incident as "a detention 
17 
only, not an arrest" based on "insufficient grounds for making a criminal complaint." No criminal 
18 
charges were ever filed.

21. The officers' conduct constitutes, at minimum, the following qualifying criminal 
21 
activity under 8 U.S.C. section 1101(a)(l5)(U)(iii): false imprisonment/ unlawful criminal 
22 
restraint (Cal. Penal Code section 236); felonious assault/ battery (Cal. Penal Code section 242); 
23 
perjury (Cal. Penal Code section 118); and obstruction of justice/ fabrication of evidence (Cal. 
24 
Penal Code section 182).

B. Consequences to Plaintiff 
27 
28 
22. As a direct result of the officers' fabricated report, Plaintiff suffered incarceration at

Santa Rita Jail for approximately five days; a one-year suspension of his Class A Commercial

Driver's License (effective February 20, 2025 through February 19, 2026); loss of employment

and wages conservatively estimated at $112,000; and severe emotional distress. These

the certification request.

23. Following the incident, Plaintiff cooperated extensively and affirmatively with every

available investigative channel: (a) Plaintiff filed a formal complaint with CHP regarding the

officers' conduct; (b) Plaintiff filed a complaint with the Commission on Peace Officer Standards

and Training ("POST"), processed under Case No. PUBLIC-26-0003 71 and forwarded to CHP on

March 23, 2026; ( c) On March 26, 2026, Defendant Serrato acknowledged receipt of the

complaint by letter, assigning Dublin Area Sergeant Eric Dutra, ID 19981, as the investigator; (d)

Plaintiff preserved and produced the complete dashcam transcript, the CHP Report, the Detention

Certificate, and all supporting documentation; (e) Plaintiff participated in DMV administrative

proceedings; and (f) at no time has Plaintiff refused or failed to provide information or assistance

reasonably requested by any law enforcement agency.

24. Under California Penal Code section 679.l0(h), these facts create a "rebuttable 
21 
presumption that the victim is helpful, has been helpful, or is likely to be helpful" in the

investigation or prosecution of the qualifying criminal activity.

D. The Certification Request

26

Nonimmigrant Status Certification to Sergeant Dutra, with a copy to Defendant Serrato. The

request included: (a) a completed Form 1-918, Supplement B (unsigned, ready for signature); (b)

7 
email: "Your email has been received and your request is under review."

E. Captain Serrato's Arbitrary Denial 
13 
14 
28. On April 20, 2026 -- eleven days after receipt and well before any meaningful review 
15 
could have occurred -- Defendant Serrato issued a letter denying Plaintiffs certification request. 
16 
The letter claims that '' [a] thorough review of this incident was conducted." That statement is 
17 
demonstrably false on this record. No thorough review of a submission containing a multi-page 
18 
legal memorandum, a detailed dashcam transcript with timestamped citations, eight supporting 
19 
exhibits, and a completed Supplement B form could have been completed in eleven days by an 
20 
office simultaneously conducting an internal affairs investigation into the same officers. The 
21 
recitation of a "thorough review" was an official statement that finds no support in the record and 
22 
that was deployed to create the appearance of compliance with section 679 .10 where none 
23 
existed. 
24 
25 
29. The letter's entire substantive analysis, verbatim, states: "Recently, you requested that 
26 
the California Highway Patrol (CHP) Dublin Area certify your Form 1-918 Supplement B, U 
27 
Nonimmigrant Status Certification, stemming from an incident that occurred on November 1, 
28 
2024. A thorough review of this incident was conducted. Unfortunately, this incident does not

1 
meet the standard of qualifying criminal activity identified in Section 679 .10 of the California 
2 
Penal Code (PC), nor does it meet the standards of the Immigration and Nationality Act Section 
3 
lOl{a)(lS)(U)(iii). Additionally, this review found no substantially similar qualifying criminal 
4 
activity as defined in Section 679. l0(d) PC. Therefore, your request to certify your Form 1-918, 
5 
Supplement B, U Nonimmigrant Status Certification, was denied."

30. Defendant Serrato was not merely aware of the underlying incident -- he was formally 
8 
put on notice of the specific evidence proving his officers committed qualifying criminal activity. 
9 
Plaintiff's submission identified the precise dashcam timestamps at which each fabrication is 
10 
disproven (00:58:51, 00:59:05, 01 :00:41, 01: 10:54, 01: 11: 15). Serrato personally possessed the

dashcam recording. He personally possessed the CHP Report containing the fabricated 
12 
statements. He personally possessed the section 851.6 Detention Certificate conceding 
13 
insufficient grounds. His denial reflects not a good-faith exercise of judgment but a deliberate 
14 
refusal to engage with evidence that would require acknowledging his subordinate officers' 
15 
criminal conduct.

31. The denial is legally deficient in the following material respects: 
a. No engagement with the evidence. The denial does not address the dashcam 
recording that disproves the CHP Report. It does not address the section 851.6 Detention 
Certificate in which CHP itself conceded the arrest lacked probable cause. It does not 
address the four documented fabrications. The conclusory statement that "a thorough 
review" was conducted is belied by the absence of any substantive analysis. 
b. No element-by-element analysis. Section 679.10 requires certification when 
three elements are met: (1) the petitioner was a victim of qualifying criminal activity; (2) 
the petitioner possesses information concerning the criminal activity; and (3) the 
petitioner has been helpful or is likely to be helpful. The denial does not identify which

element Serrato found unsatisfied or explain why. 
c. Failure to apply the rebuttable presumption. Section 679.l0(h) creates a 
rebuttable presumption of helpfulness. The denial neither acknowledges this presumption 
nor identifies any evidence rebutting it. 
d. Failure to provide specific reasons. Section 679.l0(g) requires "a written 
explanation of the specific reasons for the denial." A five-sentence boilerplate that does 
not engage with any evidence does not satisfy this statutory mandate. 
e. Internal contradiction. CHP's own section 851.6 Detention Certificate 
concedes the arrest lacked justification -- yet the denial concludes, without explanation, 
that the officers' conduct does not constitute qualifying criminal activity. These positions 
are irreconcilable. 
f. Structural conflict of interest. Serrato was asked to certify that his own 
subordinate officers committed qualifying crimes. Due process requires a neutral 
decision-maker. Withrow v. Larkin, 421 U.S. 35, 47 (1975).

F. The Absence of Alternative Remedies 
21 
22 
32. There is no internal administrative appeal or grievance process under California Penal 
23 
Code section 679.10 for the denial of a U Visa certification request. USCIS cannot remedy the 
24 
absence of an executed Form 1-918, Supplement B. The denial is a final agency action with no

adequate alternative remedy.

FIRST CAUSE OF ACTION

Violation of the Fourteenth Amendment -- Substantive Due Process 
2 
(42 U.S.C. section 1983 -Against Defendant Serrato) 
3 
4 
5 
33. Plaintiff incorporates by reference all preceding paragraphs. 
6 
34. The Fourteenth Amendment prohibits state actors from depriving persons of liberty or 
7 
property without due process of law. Where a state creates a statutory framework with mandatory 
8 
procedures and ascertainable standards, a decision-maker's arbitrary and capricious refusal to 
9 
apply those standards violates substantive due process. County of Sacramento v. Lewis, 523 U.S. 
10 
833, 845-46 (1998); Shanks v. Dressel, 540 F.3d 1082, 1087 (9th Cir. 2008). 
11 
12 
35. California Penal Code section 679.10 creates a comprehensive statutory framework 
13 
governing U Visa certification. The statute uses mandatory language ("shall"), converting what 
14 
might otherwise be a discretionary act into a mandatory ministerial duty. When the statutory 
15 
elements are met and the rebuttable presumption of helpfulness is unrebutted, the certifying 
16 
official must sign -- section 679 .10 leaves no room for unfettered discretion. The statute creates a 
17 
rebuttable presumption of helpfulness (section 679. l0(h)). It requires specific written reasons for 
18 
denial (section 679. lO(g)). It mandates processing within 30 days (section 679. lOG)). The 
19 
Legislature eliminated the requirement of prosecution, conviction, or pending investigation 
20 
(section 679.lO(k)), and strengthened these obligations through AB 1261 (Stats. 2023, Ch. 679), 
21 
effective January 1, 2024. These mandatory constraints remove the "unfettered discretion" that 
22 
ordinarily defeats due process claims and create a legitimate claim of entitlement under the 
23 
Fourteenth Amendment. 
24 
25 
36. Plaintiff possesses a protected liberty interest in the meaningful application of this 
26 
statutory framework. U Visa certification is a necessary predicate to applying for lawful 
27 
immigration status, employment authorization, and protection from removal under 8 U.S.C. 
28 
section l 10l(a)(15)(U). 
Page 11

1

37. Defendant Serrato's April 20, 2026 denial was arbitrary and conscience-shocking in 
3 
that it: (a) concluded that the officers' conduct did not constitute qualifying criminal activity 
4 
despite CHP's own dashcam proving the report was fabricated and CHP's own section 851.6 
5 
Certificate conceding insufficient grounds; (b) failed to address any of the evidence submitted; ( c) 
6 
failed to identify which statutory element was unsatisfied; ( d) failed to apply the rebuttable 
7 
presumption of helpfulness; ( e) failed to provide specific written reasons as required by section 
8 
679. lO(g); (f) reached a conclusion no rational decision-maker could reach on this record; and (g) 
9 
was rendered by a structurally biased decision-maker.

12 
private interest is substantial -- U Visa certification is a gateway to lawful status and work 
13 
authorization; (b) the risk of erroneous deprivation is extreme -- the five-sentence boilerplate 
14 
engaged with no evidence; and ( c) the governmental interest in denying certification is minimal --
15 
the Supplement B is a factual certification, not a visa approval. 
16

39. As a direct and proximate result of Defendant Serrato's violation of Plaintiffs 
18 
Fourteenth Amendment rights, Plaintiff has been deprived of meaningful access to the U Visa 
19 
process, causing ongoing uncertainty regarding immigration status, inability to obtain 
20 
employment authorization and removal protections, and emotional distress.

SECOND CAUSE OF ACTION 
24 
Violation of the Fourteenth Amendment -- Procedural Due Process 
25 
(42 U.S.C. section 1983 -Against Defendant Serrato) 
26 
27 
28 
40. Plaintiff incorporates by reference all preceding paragraphs. 
Page 12 
COMPLAINT-NEWANFORBI v. SERRATO (N.D. Cal.) 
Case 4:26-cv-05953-ASK     Document 1     Filed 06/17/26     Page 12 of 21

1 
41. The Fourteenth Amendment's procedural due process protections require, at minimum, 
2 
that a state actor provide notice and a meaningful opportunity to be heard before depriving a 
3 
person of a protected liberty or property interest. Mathews v. Eldridge, 424 U.S. 319, 333 (1976). 
4 
Where a state statute creates a legitimate claim of entitlement by constraining official discretion 
5 
with mandatory language and ascertainable standards, a protected interest arises that may not be 
6 
extinguished without adequate process. Goldberg v. Kelly, 391 U.S. 254,262 (1970); Board of 
7 
Regents v. Roth, 408 U.S. 564, 577 (1972). 
8 
9 
42. California Penal Code section 679 .10 constrains the certifying entity's discretion 
10 
through mandatory language ("shall"), a rebuttable presumption of helpfulness (section 
11 
679.I0(h)), and a requirement of specific written reasons for denial (section 679.l0(g)). These 
12 
provisions create a protected interest in receiving a reasoned, individualized certification decision 
13 
that engages with the evidence and applies the statutory standards. The interest is particularly 
14 
weighty because certification is the sole gateway to a federal immigration benefit that Plaintiff 
15 
cannot obtain through any other mechanism. 
16 
17 
43. Defendant Serrato deprived Plaintiff of this protected interest without any process 
18 
whatsoever: (a) no hearing or opportunity to respond before denial; (b) no individualized 
19 
explanation identifying which statutory element was found unsatisfied; ( c) no engagement with 
20 
any evidence submitted -- the dashcam transcript, the CHP Report, the Detention Certificate, or 
21 
the legal memorandum; ( d) no application of the statutory rebuttable presumption of helpfulness; 
22 
and ( e) no mechanism for administrative review or reconsideration. The denial letter is a 
23 
five-sentence boilerplate that could have been issued without reading a single page of the 
24 
submission. 
25 
26 
44. The process afforded-- a conclusory form denial with no reasoning, no evidentiary 
27 
engagement, and no opportunity to respond -- falls far below the minimum the Constitution 
28 
requires. As a direct and proximate result, Plaintiff has been deprived of meaningful access to the 
Page 13 
COMPLAINT-NEWANFORBI v. SERRATO (N.D. Cal.) 
Case 4:26-cv-05953-ASK     Document 1     Filed 06/17/26     Page 13 of 21

1 
U Visa certification process without constitutionally adequate procedures.

4 
THIRD CAUSE OF ACTION 
5 
Violation of the First Amendment - Retaliation for Protected Petitioning Activity 
6 
(42 U.S.C. section 1983-Against Defendant Serrato) 
7 
8 
9 
45. Plaintiff incorporates by reference all preceding paragraphs. 
10 
46. The First Amendment, as applied to the states through the Fourteenth Amendment, 
11 
protects the right to petition the government for redress of grievances. This protection extends to 
12 
filing complaints with law enforcement agencies, filing civil lawsuits against government 
13 
officials, and participating in oversight processes such as POST investigations. Borough of 
14 
Duryea v. Guarnieri, 564 U.S. 379, 387 (2011); Soranno's Gasco, Inc. v. Morgan Hill Unified 
15 
Sch. Dist., 874 F.2d 1310, 1314 (9th Cir. 1989). To state a retaliation claim, Plaintiff must allege 
16 
that he engaged in constitutionally protected activity; that Defendant took an adverse action 
17 
against him; and that the protected activity was a substantial or motivating factor for the adverse 
18 
action. Pinard v. Clatskanie Sch. Dist. 6J, 467 F .3d 755, 770 (9th Cir. 2006). 
19 
20 
4 7. Plaintiff engaged in extensive constitutionally protected activity prior to the April 20, 
21 
2026 denial: (a) filing a formal citizen complaint with the California Highway Patrol regarding 
22 
Officers Meza-Gonzalez and Melano; (b) filing a complaint with the Commission on Peace 
23 
Officer Standards and Training, docketed as Case No. PUBLIC-26-000371; (c) filing the 
24 
Alameda County Superior Court tort action (Case No. 26CV168913) on February 4, 2026; (d) 
25 
filing the Eastern District of California civil rights action (Case No. 2:25-CV-01460-DC-CSKf) 
26 
on May 27, 2025; and (e) submitting the April 9, 2026 certification request itself, which attached 
27 
the dashcam transcript, the CHP Report, and documented the officers' fabrications in detail. 
28

before he issued the denial. Serrato's own letter dated March 26, 2026 expressly acknowledges

receipt of Plaintiffs POST/citizen complaint and states that Serrato "assigned Dublin Area 
4 
Sergeant Eric Dutra, ID 19981, as the assigned investigator." This is not an inference of

subordinate officers and that an active investigation into his command was underway when

Plaintiff submitted the certification request just two weeks later.

the most natural explanation for the denial:

23, 2026. Serrato assigned an investigator on March 26. Plaintiff submitted the 
certification request on April 9. Serrato denied it on April 20 -- eleven days later --
without any substantive analysis. 
c. Concrete institutional incentive. Certifying the Supplement B would have 
required Serrato, as Commander, to officially attest under penalty of perjury that his 
subordinate officers committed qualifying criminal activity -- including perjury, false 
imprisonment, and felonious assault -- precisely while CHP was defending those same

of any legitimate justification supports the inference that the stated reason was pretextual 
and the actual motivation was retaliatory. Nieves v. Bartlett, 587 U.S. 391,406 (2019) 
(absence of legitimate basis strengthens inference of retaliatory motive). 
e. Conffict of role. Serrato simultaneously occupied two incompatible roles --
supervisor of the accused officers and certifier of whether they committed qualifying 
crimes against Plaintiff. The structural conflict made impartial decision-making 
impossible and made retaliation the path of least resistance. 
11 
50. A reasonable person in Plaintiffs position would be deterred from engaging in further

protected activity by Defendant's conduct. The denial communicates that complainants who

17

FOURTH CAUSE OF ACTION 
22 
Declaratory Relief (28 U.S.C. sections 2201-2202) 
23 
(Against Defendant Serrato in His Official Capacity) 
24 
25

52. Plaintiff incorporates by reference all preceding paragraphs. 
27 
53. An actual controversy exists between Plaintiff and Defendant Serrato regarding 
28 
whether the April 20, 2026 denial complied with constitutional and statutory standards, and

whether Plaintiff is entitled to a new certification decision that applies the correct standards to the

evidence in CHP's own possession.

54. Plaintiff is entitled to a judicial declaration that: (a) the April 20, 2026 denial violated

the Fourteenth Amendment's substantive due process protections by reaching a conclusion no

rational decision-maker could reach on this record; (b) the April 20, 2026 denial violated the

and (h); (c) the April 20, 2026 denial violated the First Amendment by retaliating against Plainti

19 
right to non-arbitrary decision-making by state officials exercising mandatory statutory duties is

clearly established. Shanks v. Dressel, 540 F.3d 1082 (9th Cir. 2008). The right to be free from 
21 
First Amendment retaliation for petitioning the government is clearly established. Borough of

Duryea v. Guarnieri, 564 U.S. 379 (2011); Hartman v. Moore, 541 U.S. 250 (2006). The specific 
23 
statutory requirements of California Penal Code section 679.10 -- mandatory certification 
24 
language, rebuttable presumption, specific-reasons requirement -- gave Defendant fair notice that 
25 
a boilerplate denial ignoring all evidence and all statutory standards would violate Plaintiffs 
26 
constitutional rights. An official can be on notice that his conduct violates established law even in 
27 
novel factual circumstances where the violation is obvious. Hope v. Pelzer, 536 U.S. 730, 741 
28 
(2002).

28. On April 20, 2026 - eleven days after receipt and well before any meaningful review
could have occurred - Defendant Serrato issued a letter denying Plaintiffs certification request.
The letter claims that "[a] thorough review of this incident was conducted." That statement is
demonstrably false on this record. No thorough review of a submission containing a multi-page

office simultaneously conducting an internal affairs investigation into the same officers. The
recitation of a "thorough review" was an official statement that finds no support in the record and
that was deployed to create the appearance of compliance with section 679.10 where none
existed.

34. The Fourteenth Amendment prohibits state actors from depriving persons of liberty or
property without due process of law. Where a state creates a statutory framework with mandatory
procedures and ascertainable standards, a decision-maker's arbitrary and capricious refusal to
apply those standards violates substantive due process. County ofSacramento v. Lewis, 523 U.S.

35. California Penal Code section 679.10 creates a comprehensive statutory framework
governing U Visa certification. The statute uses mandatory language ("shall"), converting what
might otherwise be a discretionary act into a mandatory ministerial duty. When the statutory
elements are met and the rebuttable presumption of helpfulness is unrebutted, the certifying
official must sign - section 679.10 leaves no room for unfettered discretion. The statute creates a
rebuttable presumption of helpfulness (section 679.10(h)). It requires specific written reasons for
denial (section 679.10(g)). It mandates processing within 30 days (section 679.10(j)). The
Legislature eliminated the requirement of prosecution, conviction, or pending investigation

ordinarily defeats due process claims and create a legitimate claim of entitlement under the
Fourteenth Amendment.

41. The Fourteenth Amendment's procedural due process protections require, at minimum,
that a state actor provide notice and a meaningful opportunity to be heard before depriving a
person of a protected liberty or property interest. Mathews v. Eldridge, 424 U.S. 319, 333 (1976).
Where a state statute creates a legitimate claim of entitlement by constraining official discretion
with mandatory language and ascertainable standards, a protected interest arises that may not be
extinguished without adequate process. Goldberg v. Kelly, 397 U.S. 254, 262 (1970); Board of

679.10(h)), and a requirement of specific written reasons for denial (section 679.10(g)). These
provisions create a protected interest in receiving a reasoned, individualized certification decision
that engages with the evidence and applies the statutory standards. The interest is particularly
weighty because certification is the sole gateway to a federal immigration benefit that Plaintiff
cannot obtain through any other mechanism.
